ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian احمق (ahmaq), from Arabic أَحْمَق (ʔaḥmaq).
Oblique form of ऐसा (aisā, “of this kind; in this manner”).

From Prakrit कम्मावेइ (kammāvei, “earns, works”), from older *कर्मापयति (karmāpayati), derived from Sanskrit कर्मन् (karman), whence Hindi कर्म (karm) and काम (kām). By surface analysis, काम (kām) + -आना (-ānā). Cognate with Odia କମାଇବା (kamāibā), Gujarati કમાવું (kamāvũ), Bengali কামানো (kamanō), Sindhi ڪَمَائِڻُ (kamāiṇu) / कमाइणु (kamāiṇu), Punjabi ਕਮਾਉਣਾ (kamāuṇā), Nepali कमाउनु (kamāunu), Marathi कमावणे (kamāvṇe).

Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀕𑀮 (gala) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit गल (gala). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷel- (“throat”). Cognate with Latin gula (“throat”), English gullet, and Persian گلو (galu, “throat”). Cognate with Konkani गळो (gaḷo), Marathi गळा (gaḷā).
